is a small door on the nose of Air Force One that no airliner has. It covers a fuel socket, and it is there for one day: the day the United States is under nuclear attack. This video follows what the VC-25A (a rebuilt Boeing 747-200B) is built to do on that day. It leaves without airport equipment: its own stairs unfold from the lower deck. Its electronics are hardened against the electromagnetic pulse of a nuclear blast: about 238 miles of wiring, twice that of a normal 747, all of it shielded, so the pulse runs along the shield into the airframe instead of into the equipment. From the communications center behind the cockpit the president can command from the air. And when the 7,800 miles of its own fuel run out, the door opens: a tanker lowers its boom, the boom operator lying in the tanker\x27s tail flies it into the socket, latches lock it, and fuel flows at about 900 gallons a minute. One KC-135 can give away 200,000 lb at most; these tanks hold about 359,000 lb, so it takes more than one. Food for 2,000 meals, a doctor and a fold-out operating table are already on board. It has been in service since 1990, and that day has never come.\\n\\n3D model credits:\\nAircraft: \\\x22Air Force One\\\x22 by agreene (Sketchfab user davidre), CC BY 4.0 - \x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22https:\/\/sketchfab.com\/3d-models\/air-force-one-a3512cd0cf5e4e18b1d6d2f9ea9dcffa\x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22\\n  (exterior only; the landing gear, the airstairs, the refuelling receptacle and its doors, the cut-aways, the whole interior, the KC-135 tanker with its boom and boom pod, the cable and the avionics box were modelled for this video)\\nPeople: Microsoft Rocketbox Avatar Library (MIT License) - \x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22https:\/\/github.com\/microsoft\/Microsoft-Rocketbox\x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22\\nMaterials and small props: Poly Haven (CC0) - \x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22https:\/\/polyhaven.com\x22\x7d,\x7b\x22text\x22:\x22\\nSky: \\\x22Qwantani Late Afternoon (Pure Sky)\\\x22 HDRI, Poly Haven (CC0)\\nMount Rainier: elevation from the USGS 3D Elevation Program, imagery from the USGS Imagery Only base map (The National Map). Map services and data available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program (public domain).\\nEarth: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation and cloud layer (NASA Earth Observatory \/ Reto Stockli, public domain)\\n\\nWhat is exact and what is not:\\nThe landing gear follows Boeing\x27s \\\x22747 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning\\\x22 (D6-58326). The position of the forward airstair follows official photographs; how its door and the folded stair are stowed inside is not public, so that part is plain and generic. The rooms follow the published deck plan; no interior drawings of the VC-25A are public, so furniture and equipment are typical of their kind. The inside of the refuelling receptacle is not public: the latches are drawn as a schematic. The pulse, the currents, the missile tracks, the range line, the radio beams, the fuel dots and the fuel volumes are schematic glows; the pulse takes seconds on screen instead of billionths of a second. The avionics box and the cable are generic hardware, not a specific unit of this aircraft. Starfish Prime (July 9, 1962): the burst is shown 400 km above Johnston Atoll; the line to Honolulu is 1,328 km (825 miles) long; many sources give \\\x22about 900 miles\\\x22.\\n\\nSound: real
